authority_note.documentation_rule: Human-readable pin statements elsewhere (integrations/*/README.md, docs/engine_setup.md) must cite this file and must not restate commits. On any disagreement, this file wins.
authority_note.dual_identity: Forge carries two distinct identities that must never be conflated. secondary_engine.commit is the Rules-Core authority (the engine identity the bridge reports and Rules qualification binds to). secondary_engine.bridge_source is the materialization source actually cloned and built (repository, exact commit, and the Rules-Core base commit it must descend from). The bridge source contains the Rules Core plus additive bridge surfaces; it is not a new Rules-Core version.

authority_note.pin_authority: This file (config/rules_engines.json) is the sole machine-readable authority for current engine pins: primary_engine.commit and secondary_engine.commit.

role_terminology.primary_engine: Engine under active integration (validated B4-D bridge surface). NOT a selected architecture leader and NOT a Production Provider.
role_terminology.rename_policy: Do not rename primary_engine/secondary_engine keys: they are runtime-contract fields consumed by src/commander_lab/technical_truth.py, scripts/run_external_b4f_*.py and .github/workflows/release-artifacts.yml. Terminology changes belong in documentation, not in schema renames.
role_terminology.secondary_engine: Differential candidate backend under investigation. NOT a runner-up selection.
role_terminology.selection_truth: ARCHITECTURE_FREEZE = NOT CLAIMED; PRODUCTION_PROVIDER = NOT SELECTED. provider_decision=NO_PROVIDER_READY, current_runtime.provider_selected=false, current_runtime.production_provider=null. No engine is production-selected until the provider release gate passes and a Freeze workstream records the decision.

historical_phase85.note: Preserved only for Phase 8.5 provenance; not current provider truth.

primary_engine.role: real pinned XMage B4-D bounded bridge for deck import, Commander game start, live state observation, current-priority legal-action handoff, fail-closed targetless/nonmodal action submission, external audit event export and explicit per-game lifecycle cleanup; complete external game control remains incomplete

secondary_engine.commit_meaning: ANCESTRY BASELINE ONLY. This is the pristine-upstream Forge release the Commander-Lab fork is based on, NOT the engine that executes. See engine_identity_pb09 for the engine that actually runs. Do not use this field to attribute behaviour to a running engine.

bridge_source.role: the bridge inside the fork, distinct from the engine commit

engine_identity_pb09.confusion_forbidden: These four commits are distinct. Ancestry is not identity, a descendant is a different tree, and a bridge commit is not an engine commit. None of these fields licenses reporting a result observed on one as evidence for another.

executing_engine.role: THE ENGINE THAT ACTUALLY RUNS. Lab-modified code; not pristine upstream.

native_suite_execution_root.note: a suite executed at this WSR20/WSR24 descendant must not be attributed to the fork head; the qualification runner fails closed on the divergence rather than crediting the recorded identity
native_suite_execution_root.role: WHAT THE BOUND NATIVE SUITES EXECUTE AT. Neither the fork head nor the upstream baseline.

upstream_baseline.note: no exact pristine upstream checkout with proven provenance has been established, so upstream behaviour is UNKNOWN and must never be described as observed or compared against the fork as if it were measured
upstream_baseline.role: ANCESTRY ONLY. Not the engine under test, and not verified pristine.

secondary_engine.role: candidate provider; PARTIAL real evidence, not production-selected

truth_boundary: B4-D is external_rules_engine evidence for real pinned XMage deck import, Commander construction/start, live state observation, current-priority decision/legal-action handoff, real priority passing, stale decision/action rejection, bounded submission-ready targetless/nonmodal action execution including a real Rograkh commander cast, an externally exportable monotonic bridge audit event stream with action/decision identity and pre/post state hashes, and explicit per-game XMage lifecycle cleanup/reuse. The audit stream covers real bridge/XMage lifecycle and externally controlled action boundaries; it is not claimed to be an exhaustive raw internal XMage GameEvent tap. Globally complete legal-action enumeration and action submission remain unproven because target, mode, choice and combat classes are incomplete. Mulligan, seed-control, replay and complete production game-loop coverage remain unproven. This is not win-rate evidence and does not make XMage a production-ready provider.
